# THE WONDROUS BOOK OF ZOHAR

<insert>(17) The Book of Zohar <note>original Latin: "Liber Zohar"</note></insert>

### Portion of Genesis <note>original: Parashat Bereshit</note>

**In the beginning** <note>Hebrew: "Bereshit"</note>, the King’s decree engraved an engraving into the supernal purity. A <term>scintillating flame<note>original Aramaic: "Butzina de-Kardinuta." Often translated as the "Lamp of Darkness," it represents a powerful, primordial light that is too bright to be seen, acting as the first catalyst of creation.</note></term> emerged from the concealment of concealments, from the mystery of the <term>Infinite<note>original: "Ein Sof," the boundless, unknowable essence of God before any manifestation or creation.</note></term>. Like a mist in a fog, it was fixed in a ring—neither white nor black, neither red nor green, nor any color at all. When the measurement began, it produced colors to shine inward. Inside the lamp, a spring emerged, from which colors were painted below. Hidden within the concealment of the Infinite, it split and yet did not split; its ether was not known at all until, from the pressure of its splitting, a single, hidden supernal point shone. Beyond that point, nothing is known. For this reason, it is called "Beginning" <note>Reshit</note>, the first utterance of all. "And the wise shall shine as the <term>brightness<note>original: "Zohar." The title of the book is taken from this word in Daniel 12:3, referring to the primordial radiance of creation.</note></term> of the firmament, and those who turn many to righteousness, etc." The Zohar of the concealment of concealments struck the ether, which was unknown and did not shine <unclear>in it</unclear>. Within this point, this "Beginning" expanded and made a palace for its glory and its praise. There it sowed holy seed to give birth for the benefit of the world. And this secret is: "the holy seed is its stump" <note>A reference to Isaiah 6:13.</note>. The Zohar that sowed seed for its glory is like the seed of the living Letter Aleph. And with it, <unclear>it built</unclear> that palace, and this palace is called <term>Elohim<note>A primary Hebrew name for God. In Kabbalah, this name represents the "palace" or vessel that contains the primordial light of creation.</note></term>.

<summary>This page contains the iconic opening passage of the Zohar, describing the mystical origins of the universe through the "scintillating flame" and the emergence of the "Infinite" into a point of light that forms a divine palace. It explains how the name of God (Elohim) and the concept of "Beginning" relate to these primordial, hidden emanations.</summary>
<keywords>Zohar, Bereshit, Genesis, Kabbalah, Ein Sof, Butzina de-Kardinuta, Elohim, Creation, Mysticism, Emanation</keywords>

And further it was revealed that at the time when **In the beginning [He] created** <note>original: *Bereshit Bara*</note>, that existence was established for them as the life of the Lord. And this Greatness is this **Palace** <term>Palace<note>Aramaic: *Heikhal*. In Kabbalistic thought, this represents the Sefirah of *Binah* (Understanding), which acts as a celestial structure or womb that receives the divine seed of creation.</note></term>; God engraved a law, and this spirit is "In the beginning [He] created."

The command of the **Radiance** <term>Radiance<note>Aramaic: *Zohar*. The title of the book and a term for the primordial light that emanates from the Divine.</note></term> emerges and rises for its task, to be cloaked in spirit and to be crowned within its body. Regarding the Radiance, it is written: *“The Lord is to me”* <note>original: *H' L'*</note>; by the word it is written, "He created it and he lived," as it is written: **And God created** <note>Genesis 1:21</note>. For them, the beginning of the path is the Radiance, the spirit of the first **Beginning** <note>original: *Bereshit*</note> of all. **I Shall Be** <note>Hebrew: *Ehyeh*. The Divine Name revealed to Moses at the burning bush, representing the hidden potential of God.</note> came from it, holiness emerged from within.

It emerged in the storms of God, and it emerged in the storm of **Who** <note>Hebrew: *Asher*. This refers to the middle part of the Divine Name *Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh* (I Am That I Am).</note>. The Palace made an **Eye** <note>original: *Ayin*</note> to hold the spirit of the Beginning, which is the mystery that emerged from the Beginning. And when it was established and built, the **Point** and the **Palace** were as one.

The "Priest of Beginning" <note>The Zohar often rearranges the letters of *Bereshit* to form *Berit Esh* (Covenant of Fire) or *Be-Reishit* (The Priest of the Beginning).</note> includes the Beginning; this is the **Ancient One** <term>Ancient One<note>Aramaic: *Atika*. A reference to *Keter*, the highest and most ancient of the divine emanations, representing the Divine Will.</note></term>, perfect in **Wisdom** <note>original: *Chokhmah*</note>. It was built to establish the letter *Nun* <note>The letter *Nun* in Kabbalah often symbolizes the Palace or the feminine aspect of divinity.</note>, which is the Palace. He engraved the snare and the point of peace, engraving the Head of all. 

This was created in the spirit of the Beginning for the sake of life, all as one in a single unity, until this reached the **Foundation** <term>Foundation<note>Hebrew: *Yesod*. The ninth Sefirah, which acts as the "procreative" organ of the divine realm, funneling light into the world below.</note></term> at the end. It was sown to establish the work of the Priest. God engraved the standing of the Radiance, as it is written: *“And they did so”* <note>Genesis 1:7</note>; like smoke from a beast for the lights. The standing emerged among them for the restoration of those who are the **holy seed**. And until now, it has not been diminished or withheld from the eyes of the overseer. This is the law of God for every joy of the whole Beginning. 

Afterward, we saw the heavens for life, and **five living creatures** <note>original: *chamesh chayon*. A reference to the celestial beings (Chayot) described in the vision of Ezekiel.</note> hung from the depths, and the desire was sown—the snare, the eye, and the firmament. These "living creatures" are the breath of the spirit of the Radiance, which emerged from the depths and the feminine holiness of the point. They are like the fine dust of the Palace, the spirit in which they rest. 

Go out to the law and be filled! This is **Justice** <note>original: *Tzedek*. Often associated with the Sefirah of *Malkhut* (Kingship/Kingdom).</note>. To be crowned as one spirit, a single voice emerges in a single field. In the storm that emerged, the **Daughter** <note>A term for the *Shekhinah*, the divine presence on earth.</note> came forth, according to the measure that was already established.

### In the **Zohar**, portion of **Pinhas**, page 73: 

The **Firmament** <term>Firmament<note>Hebrew: *Raki'a*. In Kabbalistic thought, the firmament is not just the sky, but a spiritual boundary or "screen" that filters the intense light of the infinite so it can be received by the lower worlds without destroying them.</note></term> exists for the sparkling within the spark of the eye of those who see <note>original: *Chazin*. This refers to the prophets or sages who possess mystical vision.</note>, who spread out as they move and stand within change.

**"And those who turn many to righteousness"** <note>Daniel 12:3</note>—this verse is used to create a passage regarding a well-spring, and so on. In this way, to look upon it, **"they shall shine"** <note>original: *Yazhiru*</note> for the sake of **Arrangement** <term>Arrangement<note>Hebrew/Aramaic: *Tikun*. The "rectification" or "ordering" of Divine lights into stable patterns or "vessels" that can sustain existence.</note></term> and beauty.

And the matter is like a portion in a well-spring within the spirit that is filled by its ascents through the ears. Judges stand beneath it; **Wisdom** <term>Wisdom<note>Hebrew: *Chochmah*. The first spark of intellect and the second of the ten Sefirot (Divine emanations).</note></term> is everything, and every level is found to be elevated in a firm wall. Silence reigns in their kingdom, and the **Kingdom** <term>Kingdom<note>Hebrew: *Malchut*. The final Sefirah, representing the physical world and the manifestation of Divine sovereignty.</note></term> is a thousand-fold in its ascent.

At times, they weigh a word and a spirit, for a firm spirit above stands as one. Two "weak" ones in ascent—**"bread shall come"**: it is written regarding the **Deficiency** <term>Deficiency<note>Hebrew: *Chesron*. In Kabbalah, a "deficiency" or "lack" is not a negative flaw but a vacuum or "vessel" (Keli) that must exist so that the Divine light has a place to enter and dwell.</note></term> of both of them above.

Worldly ascents are within: this **Deficiency** is the **Arrangement** of the world; it shall be seen from the world. For an ascent that is narrow for it is like a "thorn" <note>original: *Kotz*. Often refers to the "tip of the letter Yud," representing the most infinitesimal point of the Infinite.</note> that raises it; it is firm and stands as a resting place.

And the word does not stand until it rises through the Divine **Will** <note>original: *Re'uta*</note> above to establish the whole. It is like the matter that supports the evening below the world; it is complete within it, yet it does not stand until it is above, through the will of the one **Radiance** <note>original: *Zohar*</note>. Then Solomon <note>or "the Peace," a reference to the Sefirah of Tiferet or the completion of the spiritual structure</note> shall be built, and all is hidden and examined for vision.

The first **Radiance** shines, and it is entirely the **Kingdom**, and this spirit is a thin horn in his spirit, in him, and for him. This is the vision of the ascent... and the one who influences **"shall shine as the Radiance of the Firmament."** Those who see stand and support from outside the **Deficiency** that spreads out. Colors stand, and a few fragments are exchanged, as in the parable of the drops.

<margin>
**Thus**
</margin>

In this way, in every positive commandment of the pious, there is **Deficiency** and support, both hidden and revealed; this is the whole. Like wheat in the dust, **"they shall shine"**—this refers to **Wisdom and Understanding** <note>original: *Chu"m*, an abbreviation for Chochmah and Binah</note>. They shall shine and not be burdened for the eyes, and they are filled within that **Deficiency** by that **Wisdom** in the **Radiance** of the **Firmament**, which stands upon the visionaries and spreads out like honey and tears.

<meta>Continuity: Following the previous page’s discussion on the "Point" of creation and the spiritual firmament, this page explores the "Eyes of Mercy" and the movement of the Divine Spirit during the initial stages of Genesis, specifically focusing on how the "Holy Ancient One" (Atika Kadisha) radiates grace into the world.</meta>

Concerning all these holy pious ones of the Most High, it is said three times, and this is learned as the laws of the letters <note>original: *be-otiot*. In Kabbalistic tradition, the very shapes and combinations of Hebrew letters are seen as the "DNA" of creation.</note>. ### Marriage Contract (Ketubah)
#### Ferrara, 1676

On the **first day of the week** <note>Sunday</note>, the twenty-eighth day of the month of **Kislev**, in the year five thousand four hundred and thirty-seven from the creation of the world <note>corresponding to December 1676</note>, according to the reckoning we use here in **Ferrara**, the city which sits upon the **river Po** and near well water. 

How the dear and pleasant young man, **Mr. Benjamin**, known as the son of the late **Mr. Isaac Zalman of Forli**, said to **Ms. Rachel**, the daughter of the late, noble, and exalted **Mr. Mordechai of Viterbo**: 

"You are my bride from Heaven; be my wife according to the **law of Moses and Israel** <note>original: *kedat Moshe ve-Yisrael*; the standard formula for a Jewish marriage</note>. And I, with Heaven's help, will work for, honor, nourish, and support you, in the manner of Jewish men who work for, honor, nourish, and support their wives in truth. And I give you the marriage gift of your maidenhood, two hundred silver **zuz** <note>original: *zuzi matan*; a standard statutory amount in marriage contracts</note> which are due to you according to the Torah, as well as your food, clothing, and necessities, and I will live with you as a husband in the way of all the earth." 

And **Ms. Rachel** <term>may she be blessed among women</term> <note>original Hebrew abbreviation: *taf-kaf-alef* (tevorakh mi-nashim ohel)</note> consented and became his wife. This is the **dowry** that she brought to him from her father’s house: the sum of **five hundred and forty ducats** <note>original: *ducati*; a gold coin used across Europe</note>, valued at seven **lire** <note>original: *lit’*; local Italian currency</note> per ducat in the currency of the country. 

And thus said **Mr. Benjamin**, our groom: "I have received these one hundred and forty ducats into my hand, and I have taken them upon myself as a loan and a debt. As for the remaining five hundred ducats, they shall be under the responsibility and the strength of this **Ketubah** <note>original: *shtar ketubah*; the marriage contract document</note> according to all the customary conditions of marriage contracts used in this place." 

Furthermore, he added of his own free will, and increased for her beyond the core amount of the Ketubah, the sum of **five hundred and forty ducats** at the aforementioned value. The total sum of the dowry and the addition is **one thousand and eighty ducats** at the aforementioned value, excluding the bedding, her wedding garments, and the jewelry belonging to her person. 

And thus said **Mr. Benjamin**, our groom: "The responsibility and the weight of this marriage contract, dowry, and addition, I take upon myself and my heirs after me, to be paid from all the best of my property and possessions that I have under all the heavens—those which I have acquired and those which I may acquire in the future. All property, whether it has a guarantee <note>real estate</note> or does not have a guarantee <note>movable property</note>, shall be responsible and serve as security to pay from them this marriage contract, dowry, and addition. This applies even to the **cloak on my shoulders**, whether during my life or after my death, from this day and forever." 

The responsibility and the weight of this marriage contract, dowry, and addition were accepted by **Mr. Benjamin**, our groom, with the weight and strength of all marriage contracts, dowries, and additions customary among the daughters of Israel, made according to the enactment of our **Sages of blessed memory**. This is not to be regarded as a mere legal formality <note>original: *asmakhta*; a promise made without full intent</note> nor as a mere template of a document. 

We have performed the **act of legal acquisition** <note>original: *kinyan*; a formal ritual, usually involving the grasping of a handkerchief, to finalize a contract</note> from **Mr. Benjamin**, our groom, for **Ms. Rachel** (the aforementioned <term>may she be blessed among women</term>), using an instrument fit to perform an acquisition. 

**Everything is valid and established.**

<summary>This document is a formal marriage contract (Ketubah) from Ferrara, Italy, dated 1676, between Benjamin of Forli and Rachel of Viterbo. It details the financial obligations, dowry values in ducats and lire, and the legal guarantees provided by the groom to ensure the bride's financial security.</summary>

### On the Nature of Time and the Structure of the Worlds

Perhaps after we have explained its parts, and each individual part and what follows them, and we have explained and understood them—and before we move on to the second part—it is necessary to explain according to our method (so that we may know, observe, and act when practical application is required) the signs of the seasons, the change of the cycles, the times of the year, and the variations and transformations according to the **Zodiac** <note>original: *galgal ha-mazalot*; literally "the wheel of the constellations"</note> throughout each day and its rotation. 

From this rotation, the years of the second are drawn and supported for the sake of counting and the arrangement of its duration. This knowledge is spread across every language, and the Hebrew language has its portion just like the others. Therefore, we have begun with the matter of time from the perspective of **temperament** <note>original: *ha-mezag*; referring to the medieval and early modern concept of the "mixture" of elements or humors that govern nature and health</note> together with it, and we have begun to say: The temperament was established into seven of the parts from the side of all those who study it.

It is necessary, at the time when all its vitality is for us, so that it may be a law for the nature within us, that he should write of this matter. In the writing of the law, a tiny bit of the **structure of the worlds** <note>original: *takhunat ha-olamot*; a term referring to astronomy and the mechanical layout of the cosmos</note> is explained. From these, we shall arrange the celestial influence from time to time and the explanation of His absolute power time after time, as the Sages determined what their eyes beheld regarding the inclination toward this or that. I mean to say:

->**And God said: "Let the waters be gathered..."** [Genesis 1:9]<-

**Let [them] be gathered**—meaning, they are collected in a group to a number of "minutes" of the water <note>The author is using a wordplay on the Hebrew root *K-V-H* (gathering) and perhaps connecting it to measurements of time or quantity</note> to build <unclear>as a count to fence in</unclear> the individual point, for they are all in their rotation below, and to lay down the vapors below. And in their movement, there are six [parts] in the time of the word of the One, by His will over the heights; and He is the most singular thing of all, within the whole of everything. And they were gathered and stood to find pleasure upon it, the Heavens.

And we shall contemplate the soul from the Lord—which is complete—from under the heavens. We shall measure and establish for it a law of weeks and times and the changes found here. And we shall contemplate the words: "To the Lord he shall call" and all the other Sages. And behold, we are at the end of the actions when we desired some of the sayings. To Him there is one place, for He is the Guide who makes known the changes within them, to give thanks and to say that from Him His ray of light shall be clarified, and all the worlds below, to show them as is proper. And each for itself shall strengthen its caution in His ways.

### The Seal of the Heart and the Governance of Wholeness

The connection of the **seal** <note>original: *chotam*; likely referring to the "Seal of Solomon" or the divine imprint on the soul</note> continued in its **wholeness** <note>original: *shlemah*; also a wordplay on the name Solomon (*Shlomo*)</note> until the end of his life. And if we should slumber in His wisdom within the heart, it is with a single voice without end or limit, to sustain the whole within the heart—even through the changing of its facets. One who observes this matter beautifully will not be defeated, but will hold fast to the ultimate purpose of all complete existence. By the **governance** <note>original: *hanhaga*; a technical term in Jewish philosophy for both divine providence and the self-regulation of the soul</note> of this sealing, one shall lead and act upon the seal of the heart. Let these things be complete, clinging and strong together, lest—Heaven forbid—they be destroyed or undermined. Rather, let them be as one in a very high degree. 

It shall be in the **Infinite** <note>original: *Ein Sof*; the Kabbalistic term for God as He exists prior to any manifestation</note> of the extremities, lest the **distance of uprightness** <note>original: *merchak ha-yosher*; a term likely referring to the deviation from the middle path or the straight line of divine light</note> becomes a distance toward death. Our God's hand is upon this, and according to His will, it finds favor in the eyes of the Name, may He be blessed. 

And what is this distance? Lest one be removed to the "Camp of Solomon"—referring to those who fall into his camps—a doubtful distance toward death. The meaning of being "sealed" is truly to provide for the needs of **Rachel** <note>original: *Rachel*; in mystical thought, Rachel often symbolizes the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence) or the physical world that needs to be sustained by the "Seal"</note> and the hope of the believer, which fills their possessions. This is only for one of high degree, one who is beautiful in their standing. 

Therefore, he is strengthened in his wrath by the fortification of the **commandments** <note>original: *mitzvot*</note>, established, prepared, and known. Lest the distance of uprightness—the doubt of light in his camp—should cause them to vanish, He shall send His vision. It is a distance toward death for their camps and their portion. Their portion shall be for the Name... divided above as one to give life. And the hand of the ancient one... his wisdom and his governance shall not be found lacking. 

The portion of **wholeness** <note>original: *Shlomo*</note> must be tested to draw out their weariness into a heart that is established, prepared, and known through the pleasantness of His commandment. It is a mystery and a secret. And he travels toward the One, heavy with the glory of His kingdom forever and ever. **Judah** <note>perhaps referring to the community of Israel or a specific lineage</note> shall be divided above in wholeness; indeed, they shall stand to be given life, and as one they shall hope for His elevation.

### The Small House and the Sprouting of the Word

And they sprout from within a **small house** <note>original: *beit katan*; in Kabbalistic thought, this often refers to the Tabernacle or the human heart as a dwelling for the Divine</note>, and this is the small house that sprouts among them, belonging to the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*; the standard Rabbinic way of referring to God</note>. All things tremble before this, and you might ask: "How is this so? And what is the reason for this joy?" ### The Measure of the Intellect and the Radiance of the Soul

And all that they find there from the portion of everyone who has acquired even a small part of the **Intellect** <term>original: *Sekhel*; in this context, the Active Intellect that connects the human mind to Divine wisdom</term> stands exactly and in full measure. ### The Investigation into the Likeness of the Spirit

->At the start of the inquiry into what constitutes the likeness of the **Spirit** <term>original: *Ruach*; the middle level of the soul, often associated with the breath, emotions, and the heart</term>, this investigation concerns that which is perceived. These investigations are situated in the final place; in such a manner, a pure light appears there. It remains with him—Heaven forbid <note>original: *chas v'shalom*; an expression used to ward off negative possibilities</note> it should ever change—along with its law, its order, its house, and the dwelling of the **Body** <term>original: *Guf*</term>.<-

When it seeks to be completed with a beautiful perfection, they are spread out, and there was no shared deficiency to its life. It settled the legal arguments and joined with the vital light to flee and to be strengthened. ### The Third Part

The third part will approach the key to these three degrees. The foundation of all wisdom is the **knowledge of Him**, may He be blessed—the Creator, blessed be His name. Regarding this degree, the proof and the sign are found in this scripture: **King Solomon**, peace be upon him <note>original Hebrew: *A"H*, an abbreviation for *alav hashalom*</note>, who instructs [one] to look into the intellects <note>abstract spiritual concepts</note>, the ladder of virtues, and the precise formulations of tradition. For in the heart of the wisdoms hidden for the knowledge of Him, may He be exalted—

King Solomon—as our Sages of blessed memory <note>original Hebrew: *Z"L*, an abbreviation for *zikhronam livrakha*</note> said: Shemaya stood to publicize his existence until they provided the parable to illustrate and bring it into being. Let the matter be sharp and connected through them, and through them, he shall have a stronghold and refuge in its appointed time. These are in my inner being and provide a foundation for the settled mind; even upon his sleep, he shall be pure, until he becomes a holy canopy for your soul. 

And you shall not lack in any place, nor shall you pass from matter to matter, as it is written in Proverbs: **"He who acts wisely in a matter shall find good"** [Proverbs 16:20]. And this is the parable of this deep custom. And what is the path to her rest? Let us be strengthened in the search for health to clarify and understand the science; and that which is clarified from the matter of his wisdom is the wisdom they established in the mouth of every man. They called these **The Work of the Chariot** <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah: The earliest tradition of Jewish mysticism, based on the prophet Ezekiel’s vision of the Divine Throne-Chariot. It deals with the deepest secrets of creation and the divine realm.</term>. And so we have learned: **Rabbi Phinehas ben Jair** <term>Rabbi Phinehas ben Jair: A famous 2nd-century sage known for his piety. He is best known for describing a "ladder" of spiritual virtues, where each quality (like caution or cleanliness) leads to a higher state, eventually reaching the Holy Spirit.</term> 

Indeed, it is written: *"God will provide for Himself"* [Genesis 22:8].

# The Purpose and the Wonders of the Kingdom

Regarding the purpose and the end of all things, from which one may survey the wonders of the **Kingdom** <term>Malchut</term> <note>the final of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations, often associated with the physical world and the presence of the Divine on Earth</note>. In this matter, there are several sections concerning how our soul is destined to be a portion of **Eternity** <term>Netzach</term> <note>the seventh Sefirah, representing endurance and victory</note>. This is also the case when the **composite being** <note>original: "ha-murkhav"; a philosophical term for the human being, who is composed of both a physical body and a spiritual soul</note> becomes a dwelling place for its home and its body; thereafter, holiness flows from the eternal source.

This is the secret of the composite nature of man, as it is written: **The Lord has made all things for His own purpose** <note>original: "Asah Adonai et kol zeh k'neged ma'anehu"—a quote from Proverbs 16:4, implying that everything in creation has a specific divine intention</note>. This occurs at a specifically designated time. Through their arrival at this realization, they achieve a holy division of sanctity. For they prayed ten times over these matters, seeking our grace from the Holy One. He chose to separate the wicked from evil, and so it is with every creature and living thing.

He works within life itself; His world is a perpetual renewal. Even those who might deny Him must acknowledge that it is holy. Thus, man is a servant within life. Consider the moment of **emanation** <term>hitpashtut</term> <note>the process by which divine light spreads or extends into the lower worlds</note>: he exists within life and vision. They become wise and holy because they prayed, lest judgment befall them. 

That specific judgment is withheld and spared for us, so that they shall not be overcome by the "shrouding" of the divine light. Each person shall be transformed through them. It is not until the proper time and the arrival of **His Messiah** that one should be stubborn; rather, one must bind oneself to the whole. Therefore, there was a period until the year 152 <note>This may refer to a shortened year (432/1672) or a specific numerical value (gematria) related to "the end"</note> for the purpose of holy division. 

And if the response is unified, not apart from the time and His Messiah, then life becomes a **crown** <note>original: "atar"</note>. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not complete the work until the appointed time of His Messiah—not even for the children who grew wise through the needs of **Abraham** <note>referring to the merit of the patriarchs</note>. Meanwhile, He worked through them, filling the lacks of all the worlds in their proper time. This is not only for the wise but for the holy children He has made. 

Let the lack suddenly cease, and may the needs of the "face of the sun" <note>likely an allegory for the revealed face of God or the Messiah</note> be met. So they concluded this section regarding the needs of the children. All their time was spent in prayer, seeking **Understanding** <term>Binah</term> and **Loving-kindness** <term>Chesed</term>. There is no new thing here, yet even those who deny the truth acknowledge the holiness resulting from their prayers. From the higher worlds, three matters descend to the lower ones, so that the Lord may look upon them with favor. From that **Time of Favor** <note>original: "Et Ratzon"; a propitious time when divine mercy is accessible</note> comes our grace; holiness does not die, but remains a holy and life-giving renewal.

### Concerning the Priests and the Hidden Teachings

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of liturgy, moving from the missing letter in the Shema mentioned on page 114 to a deeper discourse on the quality of Loving-kindness (Chesed) and how the Compassionate One (Rachmana) prepares spiritual "levels" for the blessing of the community.</meta>

**The Compassionate One** <note>original: *Rachmana*; a common Aramaic title for God used in the Talmud and Zohar, emphasizing the attribute of mercy.</note>. In the Zohar, section *Vayikra* <note>The third book of the Torah, Leviticus</note>, page 8, it is stated: [the letter] Chet (H) signifies **Mercy and Compassion** <unclear>lm</unclear> <margin>4, 36</margin>.

At every time and every season, the Holy One, Blessed be He, must join His Name with the letters **Chet (H)** and **Dalet (D)** <note>The letters Chet and Dalet are often discussed in Kabbalah; together they can hint at the word "Chad" (One) or the attributes of Grace and Judgment</note>, which relates to the rain of providence. <meta>This page continues the philosophical exploration of divine emanation, transitioning from the previous page's focus on the Alsheich’s wisdom to a structural analysis of how the Divine Will creates and sustains the universe. Because of the **Will** <note>original: *Ratzon*. And between the extension from nothingness to the outside, they are drawn by their nature. And because they are drawn, the "Will of Evil" <note>An unusual phrase, possibly referring to the *Yetzer Hara* or the lack of divine alignment.</note> is lacking, for it is not from Him; it necessitates not its own existence, except as a mere likeness of Grace, not in its true nature. Furthermore, why did they raise the concern that their rigidity might change after death? ### The Subject of the Discourse: The World to Come

The subject of this discourse concerns the **World to Come** <note>original: "עה"ב" - *Olam Ha-Ba*</note> and the intended meaning for one engaged in this work: "Every soul rests in its own assigned place."

What we receive from the outside is not known merely through its **outward appearance** <term>original: *chitzoniyut* – the external, literal, or physical dimension of a spiritual reality</term>. Those who understood the word and its fracture realized that, certainly, on our own, there are none here who truly understand. The law of "external knowledge" teaches us to learn from those who possessed unique wisdom and the power of choice.

And he revealed a wondrous perfection; in delving into these matters, the death of Abel opened a wondrous path. Regarding his perfection—and who can testify to it?—**Hezekiah** <note>The Judean King, often discussed in the Talmud for his righteousness and his relationship with mortality</note> opened this path: For whom is death significant in his very being, and for whom is it not?

Thus, death in one's being is not merely a physical act; it involves all who are prepared to know.

In the external aspect, the structure of his perfection is strong; who is truly perfect in the external aspect? There is a hint here in the external aspect. Therefore, the "death of perfection" is not mentioned in its accompanying text.

The eighteen <note>Likely referring to the eighteen blessings of the *Amidah* prayer, which corresponds to the "structure" of the spiritual self</note> are in the structure of his perfection—perfection in all. Who is he in the external aspect? And the perfection of its restoration is in the external aspect. And so it is that we have received it in the external aspect, in his perfection. 

This refers to the one who rests in the external aspect. Let there be perfection in the external aspect, according to the law of every soul that rests. Let every law of its virtues be perfection in this, above all; and every law shall be perfection. For those resting in the external aspect, we find grace in their "enveloping" from above. For this reason, in its own place, there is perfection. As it is written: **"Blessed be the Lord from world to world"** <note>Psalm 106:48</note>—this is the structure.

# The Offering of the Human Heart

## The Discourse of Rabbi Eleazar

And he set the rods <gloss>original: *va-yatzeg et ha-maklot* — which he had peeled, etc.</gloss>. Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse:

"When any man of you brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2. This verse serves as the foundation for discussing how physical acts mirror spiritual realities</note>. To you, O wisest of the wise, I come; and I stand before you to speak. A voice cries out: "Woe to those who are living yet are perfected in nothing! Woe to those who do not know and do not observe the words of the Torah!" And woe to all those who do not observe because there is no one among them who fears Heaven. 

For one who truly fears is like a soul without a body: pure, without a single speck <term>original: *kortopa* — a tiny measure or a minute blemish; in Kabbalah, it represents even the smallest deviation from purity</term>, and his words are kept in a holy case. Such people see the pure ones of the Sanctuary; they offer praise and songs of glory to the Holy One for the sake of the words of the Torah. For behold, anyone who "enters and exits" <note>A common Zoharic idiom for someone who studies the hidden depths of Torah safely</note> as is fitting, finds himself within the Torah, and no deficiency can be found in the Torah itself. 

All those souls who hover in purity, when they behold the words of the Torah, there is no one among them who does not know how to see the hidden things of the world within those words. Through them, Jerusalem is sustained. But woe to those who ignore the Torah, for when the words of the Torah demand justice for their insult before the King, those people will be punished with a bitter punishment by the one who was meant to be their help. 

### The Secret of "From You"

What is written in the Torah? "When any man of you brings an offering..." The text specifies **from you** <gloss>original: *mikem* — implying the offering must come from the person's own essence or labor</gloss>. And is this "from you" literal? For we have learned this entire teaching from many great and precious sages who are more exalted than this world. Without this "from you," no kindness <term>original: *chesed* — the divine attribute of expansive love and grace</term> is found in the world. 

How then shall they exist in the "Life of Lives" of the Holy One, blessed be He? The King, God, speaks wisdom and wise things every day to the person who is as pious as the holiness of Jerusalem. He has said: "He who comes with the Torah shall not fall into a single pious repair" <note>meaning he will not need to undergo difficult rectifications because the Torah itself protects and repairs him</note>. 

And if this day does not dwell in his heart, and he is found among those who do not see, it is so that the words of the higher worlds may rebuke him and offer praises for life. Come and see: all those who are complete and perfected are praised through these words, for they have no speck of impurity within them. All species are made complete and are established in uprightness, and the blessing from the higher world descends upon them. Peace is found in them, and the life of these pure ones is strong; everything is found exactly as it should be.

And behold, everything is one, one, one—from this side and from that. And for whoever can see into it, it is written:

->**"And he set the rods..."**<-

This refers to the patriarch Jacob, and he did this in order to return the flow of blessing to the Supernal Foundation <term>original: *Yesod* — the ninth Sephirah (divine emanation), which acts as a channel or "foundation" for all spiritual energy flowing into our world</term>.

### Portion of Vayishlach [And He Sent] Jacob

**Rabbi Yehuda** opened his discourse with the verse: *“For He shall give His angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways”* <note>Psalm 91:11</note>. This verse has been established and explained to mean that throughout the time a person is found in this world—from the very moment he emerges into life—two angels are appointed to him as one. They are sent to oversee him, one from this side and one from that side: the right and the left, male and female.

And why a female aspect? Because a human is created through both father and mother. The Holy One, blessed be He, commands these angels to be bound to the person at every single moment. How is it possible for them to be present? Because he saw another [teaching] that was established, and he saw that all life depends on this: happy is the righteous person who merits this. 

When a person walks in the [proper] paths, the angels rejoice over them. A "good" spirit is found for such a person, for he is meritorious and walks in the path of faith <note>original: *orcha de-meheimanuta* — a technical Zoharic term for the path of mystical faith and divine alignment</note>. He merits [grace] here. In this way, as a person walks, so it has been established: that [other] one, the "evil" spirit, is humbled before him. It is well said of such a person that they are paired together to serve the human being, from those who are beautiful—this one and that one—performing their duties toward him. 

They stand and cry out before the Holy One, blessed be He, concerning the nations in that world <note>The spiritual realms</note>. From them, they draw forth the vitality and the matter of the word in great abundance, just as it is appropriate. As it is written: *“And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him”* <note>Genesis 32:2</note>. 

And we see here that he was not strengthened by his own kind [alone]. There is a hint here that has been revealed: this teaches regarding the "Scapegoat" <note>original: *Azazel* — the desert spirit to whom the scapegoat was sent on Yom Kippur; here used to represent the forces of the "Other Side"</note>. We see from them [the angels] that they preceded him to erase the [accusatory] power. And Jacob, when he spoke to them... 

And the angels—from where were they called? And for what purpose? Behold, it says: **“And Jacob sent messengers before him...”** <note>Genesis 32:4. The Hebrew word *Malachim* means both "messengers" and "angels." The text is playing on the idea that Jacob sent actual spiritual beings as his envoys to Esau.</note>

### Reflections on Wisdom and the Work "Enoch from my Youth"

Truly, **Rabbi Isaac Habib** has been dear to me, as has the work *Enoch from my Youth* <note>original: *Hanoch MiNe'uray* — this could refer to a specific manuscript or a curriculum of study related to the mystical figure of Enoch/Metatron</note>, for he was engaged in the vision and in the teachings of **Rabbi Yochanan**. After I saw with clarity and understanding, investigating it thoroughly, I gained wisdom from the waters of his custom and his conduct...

Let it be seen that we hold fast from this point to that, like the chapter of the **"Houses"** <note>likely referring to a structural division of the text or a specific legal/mystical discussion regarding the "Houses" of Hillel and Shammai</note>, and this deed of... every desire of man.

His task was to see the goodness of my soul. I signed this with grace while settled, and in these words he engraved a bit of all wisdom and of all the sciences. For he is gracious... to their signature while settled. For **Isaac Habib** is among the "sons of the lodging," even among the buyers, to set his mind at ease; and I rejoiced in this, my portion. There is no part of my youth that would be a benefit to my forgetfulness <note>The author suggests that his early studies are so foundational that they cannot be forgotten or lost even as he ages</note>.

If one gives from his own kind besides what was appointed for him by his deeds, and from Heaven he was pushed aside—the poor man, in some manner, even if there is a deficiency <note>original: "חסרון" - *chesron*; a technical term in Kabbalah referring to a state of lacking or an empty vessel needing to be filled by divine light.</note> in him. -># Conduct in Dress and Dining when the Perfect One, may He be blessed, Comes to Rule Over Us<-

Regarding clothing: a man's place is reflected in his garment, and within it dwells the Sabbath, the importance of his service, and the honor of the Blessed One.
The Pious One <note>original: "החסיד" (*Ha-Chasid*), likely referring to Rabbi Judah the Pious, author of *Sefer Hasidim*</note> wrote: one's clothing should only be of a temperament that is not far from the "middle measure" <note>A reference to the Aristotelian/Maimonidean "Golden Mean" of moderation.</note>.
For Rav Yehuda said: A person should never change [his style of dress] from that of his neighbors <note>original: "לכל שביעין" — though the OCR is unclear, the rabbinic context suggests "among his peers" or "neighbors" to avoid pride or mockery.</note>, for such is the way of the pious.
Clothing is like an inn <note>original: "מלון" (*malon*)</note> that you enter for your needs. See also what we have written regarding the *Duties of the Soul* <note>original: "חובת נפש" (*Chovat Nefesh*), referring to the classic work *Chovot HaLevavot* by Bahya ibn Paquda.</note>.

And let your garments be whole and clean, and distinct when among the congregation. And in the *Order of Education* by the Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel, a 13th-century legal authority.</note> and in the *Great Book of Commandments* <term>Semag: Sefer Mitzvot Gadol, a 13th-century legal code by Rabbi Moses of Coucy</term>, it says that the body <note>original: "הג'" abbreviation for *haguf*</note> should not be soiled, and the clothing should be measured and beautiful according to the strength of one's body. These are three things that constitute "appearance."

In the First Gate of *The Pious One*, it is written that a pious man should honor his garments, but he should not use "garments of piety" <note>Referring to ostentatious clothing meant to signal extreme religious asceticism</note>, nor should he consider his clothing like that of a king or a sailor. For it is said: "No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your tent" <note>Psalm 91:10</note>.
Rabbi Yirmiyah explained: "No evil shall befall you" refers to the body; "nor shall any plague come near your tent" means that harmful spirits shall not damage it, nor shall weakness or sickness enter.

One should not have a portion that is more than necessary, so that it does not happen that nothing is left for the house of the orphan. All this is a command for the perfection of the soul in our time; according to our blessing, it is a great obligation, and its foundation is Loving-kindness <term>Chesed: the attribute of divine grace and benevolence</term>.

After this, one who forgets <note>or avoids</note> dangers will not be harmed by the wicked. The "eye of the wicked" shall not touch the bread, for touching the bread brings the damage of hunger—which is a division of evil—and the "evil eye" is a manifestation of divine wrath.
The pious man shall fulfill and occupy himself with the Living Essence of the Soul and the Living Essence of the Spirit <note>original: "חיה דנפש וחיה דרוח" (*Chayah de-Nefesh, Chayah de-Ruach*). These are high-level mystical grades of the human soul in Kabbalah.</note>, as it is written: "A living soul." We call the Living Essence "of the Place of the Almighty," and it is called "Rescues," for this is true vitality.

The "evil eye" is synonymous with injustice. Therefore, "uprightness" and the "congregation" are dependent on this Living Essence <note>original: "חיה" (*Chayah*)</note>. This is the wrath of anyone who exists in her kingdom but is not "whole in her body" and protected by her kingdom—this comes from the Table <note>Likely referring to the Altar or the act of eating</note>, and through it, she shall be made whole. We see elders who are occupied with their purses, and among them, those who are uplifted and do good in the congregation; but if there is an eye of oppression, it whispers within the midst of life.

<summary>This page outlines ethical and mystical guidelines for dress and dining, emphasizing moderation, cleanliness, and the avoidance of ostentation to protect the soul from spiritual harm (the "evil eye") and to facilitate divine connection.</summary>

# The Treasury of the Books of the Wars of the Lord

He rectifies the literal meaning of **Unity** <note>original: *Yichud*, the meditative practice of unifying divine attributes</note> as many stand around it to purify it for the Name. They opened and they learned: "He sent his bread outside..."

<margin>He desires</margin> for the Lord; the body shall understand and be supported from within.

A youth <note>original: *na'arit*, possibly referring to the soul or a lower spiritual level</note> should be occupied with the commandments. This is called "life for his quarters." # The Virtue of Observing the Commandments

The virtue of keeping the commandments <note>original: *shmirat hamitzvot*</note> is like one who "desires life" <note>A reference to Psalm 34:13: "Who is the man who desires life...?"</note> and shall be called holy. When it is seen that the angel departs from a person, or if his merit is unified, he lacks one angel to testify for him, as recorded in the tractate <note>Likely a reference to the Talmudic tradition that angels are created by a person's good deeds to act as advocates in the heavenly court</note>. And from where do we know that Israel has an appointed angel <note>original: *malach memuneh*</note> when they are seen by the Blessed One? For once a person departs from the world in peace, he acquires a special angel to accompany him.

Today, the pious sages <note>original: *chachamei chasidim*</note> have taught that both of them are exempt. Behold, for him, the **Evil Inclination** <term>Evil Inclination: original: *Yetzer HaRa*; the innate human impulse toward selfish or physical desires, which in mystical thought can be harnessed or transformed for spiritual growth</term> is made to live for the sake of the deeds of the Lord. He saw that he departs from the world for the sake of life, and his end is peace.

Concerning this, who is "pure of heart" <note>original: *bar levav*; see Psalm 24:4</note>? One who walks in this way before Him. Let the **Evil Inclination** be made to live; he made it into a servant for him. The Merciful One <note>original: *Rachmana*; a common Aramaic title for God</note> commanded to blind the "worker of confusion" <note>original: *oved shebush*; likely referring to the distracting power of the ego or the demonic forces that sow doubt</note>. 

The **Adversary** <note>original: *Sitna*, or Satan</note> was removed and stood alive before the **Holy One** <note>original: *Kudsha*, an abbreviation for the Holy One, Blessed be He</note>, and there was peace. He accepted the bond of the commandment <note>original: *mitzvah*</note> as a single authority, yet for all this, the Truth <note>original: *Kushta*</note> did not fully penetrate it. This is because a portion was given for a complete blessing, while the flaws were diminished.

The virtues are like joy, intended for life. The soul, though it may be lowly, shall have the **Evil Inclination** as a potion <note>original: *sam*; can mean medicine, spice, or drug. Here it implies a transformative substance</note> so that he does not die. One should not mock this before Him, because this was not yet the perfected Truth. Since the **Adversary** could not hear, the **Holy One, Blessed be He** blinded him toward them, and they were transformed. He rose and hurried to the Holy One, and the **Adversary** joined them... 

In the end, all is companionship. The **Evil Inclination** is an engraving, yet it did not remain, for at the beginning He sealed them from the world. In your house, your lineage is to be completed for life. The **Evil Inclination** was revived; a small thing or a "star" <note>A mystical metaphor for a point of light or a specific soul-spark</note> was improved before the Root <note>original: *Ikra*; the Divine Source of all things</note>. This was better than "good." 

This is what **Jacob** saw when he looked upon the face of **Esau** <note>A reference to Genesis 33:10, where Jacob tells Esau, "to see your face is like seeing the face of God." In Kabbalah, this represents the redemption and elevation of the "sparks" within the forces of Edom/Evil</note> and they were occupied with the Lord and lived.

# The Proactive Love of the Creator and the Mystery of the Garments

He adds to what he has acquired for himself. Moreover, if this were not the case, he would never set his heart toward the **love of the Creator**, blessed be He, because even a wealthy man lacks these spiritual merits. Through this, you may understand the statement of **Rabbi Yochanan**: "No man has ever done me a kindness and preceded me in it." <note>original: "מעולם לא עשה לי אדם טובה וקדמני בה"; This Talmudic sentiment (found in the Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 2:1) illustrates the sage's commitment to being the initiator of kindness or immediately reciprocating it, ensuring he remained spiritually proactive rather than reactive.</note>

This pertains to the **Pious One** <term>Pious One: original: *Chasid*; a term for one who goes beyond the strict requirements of the law to act with extra devotion and kindness</term>. What is this Pious One? This is Yochanan, a "golden lamp" <note>original: *ner zahav*; a metaphor for a luminary of Torah or a soul of high rank</note> who did not falter; he conducted himself as a "desirable lamp" and did not cease from the "table of kings" <note>A common metaphor for the pursuit of divine wisdom or high spiritual standing</note> and remained within.

Because if one has nothing with which to pay, why would he take from the longing prophet? Concerning this, it is said that the heavens are aligned against those who fear for Your sake. And when his animals were not found, he lay down and placed the **garments** <note>original: *smalot*; refers to the changes of clothes mentioned in the story of Joseph and his brothers in Genesis 45</note>. These things were distant...

And why did he find others? It is because for His **Pious One**, he went in wholeness and turned away from that [evil] path. There is one who is "wise of heart" <note>original: *maskil ha-lev*</note> who will not accept a complete reward. Why then did he make the garments? It was so that there would be joy and the eye would see a "wise deed."

But regarding these, what is written? "And afterward **Joseph**..." <note>Referencing Genesis 45</note> Joseph acted from ten perspectives; there were five and three, and all five hundred. Joseph gave a kiss to the five and a gift for the truth of the Name <note>original: *Shem*</note> corresponding to the years of the wicked. Therefore, I will make a memory of the women.

I have already stated that Jacob acted with "cunning" <note>original: *arum*; this Hebrew word is a pun, meaning both "shrewd/clever" and "naked." This relates to the sin of the ten years and the three "faces" belonging to **Understanding** <term>Understanding: original: *Binah*; the third Sephirah or divine attribute in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing the womb of creation and the processing of wisdom into thought</term>. This oppression is from the God who is blessed.

This belongs to the "High Kindness." **Rabbi Joseph** said that whoever is "spared" <note>original: *chas*; likely a wordplay on *Chasid* (Pious)</note> does not know, and a person assists him. The edges of the glory are lacking for them... from that which is sufficient and heard by every master.

### The Smallness of Simeon and the Nature of Completion

The **smallness of Simeon** <note>original: *Ketanah del Shimon*; this may refer to a specific attribute of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai or a "minor" aspect of his teachings</note>. And according to the small measure, there is a certain restraint regarding his affairs. Let it be in **silence** <note>original: *belachas*; often used to denote secret or whispered mystical teachings</note>, and this is his: he knew that he lacked nothing at all. Had he lacked, there would be no **sealing** <note>original: *chatimah*; can also mean "wedding" or "conclusion," implying a spiritual union that cannot occur in a state of deficiency</note>, for the law of separation—Heaven forbid—is a law of distance. And this is his sealing: he shall not lack, and it shall not be a lack to him.

And if he possesses an **ascent in perfection** <term>Shelimut; a state of spiritual wholeness or perfection where the soul is in total harmony with the Divine</term>, he desired it to be within the law, and it shall be truly **absorbed** within him. He shall not turn to the rejection of it, for this is the **deficiency** <term>Chisron; the mystical concept of lack or void that must be filled by divine light</term> of every virtue; finding in it the path to the completion of his lack. Let him be established in existence, preventing himself from searching for perfection in the **profane desires** <note>original: *chapetzim shel chol*; referring to worldly or non-sacred interests</note>, for everything is attached. As it is written: *The Lord shall dwell therein* [Psalm 68:17], for He took pity upon the face of His servant. These wonders in the times of the **fallen** <note>original: *defalim*; likely referring to the spiritually lowly or those in exile</note> are forgotten in their perfection.

We have no unmerited grace except that which is granted through the tranquility of the intellect with her; these are the **attained ones**. And this is not for them a matter of patience, but rather for us, in that which we find rest and become wise. And if there is no **wisdom** <term>Chokhmah; divine wisdom, the first emanation of the creative light</term>, then *they followed vanity and became vain* <note>original: *va-yelekhu acharei ha-hevel va-yehevalu*; a quote from Jeremiah 2:5, describing those who pursue illusions and become empty themselves</note>.

### On Exemption and Restitution

Simeon taught: Between the **enclosure** <note>original: *chafiah*; a covering or protective space</note> and the portion of life, one is—Heaven forbid—**exempt from paying** <term>Patur mi-leshalem; a legal term here applied to spiritual debt. It suggests that one who has reached a certain level of holiness is no longer "indebted" to the lower forces</term> to those who seek his desires. For they are the children of grace, who are together and standing upon the level of the **dwellers** <note>original: *shokhnim*</note>. In the tongue of the righteous, it is established in its decree, and thus the strength of the **soul’s foundation** is firm.

And one who is **whole** <note>original: *shalem*</note> is exempt from paying. And so, in the times of strength, he established his heart within it. For the worlds have passed, and until the beginning, he prevented the removal of his **desires for Jacob**. And this shall restore the desires to him, to be sustained from sin. According to the power of the **Heavens** <note>original: *shamayim*</note>, the logic of the enclosure is established for **all worlds** <note>original: *le-khol almin*; an Aramaic phrase meaning eternally or across all planes of existence</note>; it exists for the kingdom and for the distance. He opened and said: it is sealed within it.

## The Portion of "And it was at the End" <note>original Hebrew: Parashat Vayehi Miketz</note>

Rabbi Hiyya opened [with the verse]: "**He set an end to darkness, and for every purpose he searches out the stone of gloom and the shadow of death.**" <note>Job 28:3. The Hebrew word 'Ketz' (end) in the verse mirrors the name of the Torah portion, Miketz.</note> "He set an end to darkness" — this refers to the **End of the Left** <term>Ketz d’Smala: in Kabbalah, the "Left side" represents the attribute of strict Judgment and the source of the "Other Side" or evil forces</term>, in which darkness wraps itself at the time it descends into the world and stands before the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: Ka-Be-Hu (abbreviation for Kadosh Baruch Hu)</note> to indict. And it seeks to confuse [the world]; this is the decree of the **Destroyer** <term>Mechabla: an accusing or destructive angelic force</term>.

"He searches out" — for all the deeds of the children of men come to arouse judgment and to hinder peace. "He set an end to darkness, and for every purpose he searches out the stone of gloom and the shadow of death." These are the **Thread of Life** <note>original: Chut HaChayim; a spiritual lifeline connecting the soul to its source</note>. "He set an end to darkness, and for every purpose he searches out" — the "stone of gloom" is the "End" of the **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of spiritual impurity or evil</term>, which is their darkness and thick gloom.

And this "searching" occurs during the hour when it has permission to look upon the works of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, and to speak of the praise and the fear of the children of men, and it covers them with sleep <note>or "teeth/accusal"</note>. For this "searcher" is a commandment <note>or "assigned task"</note> before a person every day, and it searches out the presence of the **Evil Inclination** <note>original: Yeser HaRa</note>, who is "lacking in heart" and "far from the Master," and this is the "Searcher with full eyes."

And when a person looks upon his path and sees in it the [spiritual] garment that covers him, then he lives in a state of peace and is seen in the "Peace of the Future" <note>the World to Come</note>. For when one listens to the **Satan** <note>the Accuser</note> who removes peace, [then darkness] shall be established for us. For everything that is of peace belongs to the **Living** <note>original: Chayah</note>, take its life, for it lives for them in the hour when judgments are aroused from above.

And through judgment, one sees in it the "living" for them, to strengthen [them], and then the "Peace of Levi" <note>likely referring to the Covenant of Peace with the tribe of Levi</note> is with them, and peace precedes the time that he lives for them in the dwelling <note>or "Sabbath"</note>, and thus it is "The Living Being" <note>Chayta</note>. In this same manner, **Ezekiel** saw in his path "The Living" <note>Chayto</note> and the strong ones, and was commanded with the **Garment of Life**. And when a person's heart desires the words of those who are ancient in the Path of Life, then they see...

## The Mystery of the Sabbath Table and the Divine Union

The living shall praise [You] forever <note>original: "Chayim hayu yehalelu selah" — a reference to the liturgy, emphasizing that the vitality of the worlds depends on this praise</note>. ### Rabbi Yehuda Opened

When observing the morning of a single day—which is neither fully day nor [night]—there was morning for **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah: the first spark of divine intellect, often symbolized by the first light of dawn</term>, and the day became night. It is this light that illuminates the depth; it is a hint to the number seventy <note>This likely refers to the seventy years of a human life or the seventy "faces" of the Torah that illuminate the darkness</note> regarding the morning and the Sabbath.

And there was morning—and what is this great labor, and why does it come from beyond? This light passes over to the night, concerning the arrangement of death <note>original: "ma'arich hamavet" — potentially referring to the extension or postponement of mortality through spiritual practice</note>, leaving it below without its usual custom. One chooses the morning in this judgment, for the morning of Wisdom is beautiful; and if it were not so, they would not sing before Him. And there was morning—morning—for one does not engage in this [labor] except when it is morning. And what is lacking? It is not explained, but this is the case when one drinks the moisture of the morning.

The seven [lamps] did not depart at all; the radiance remained in the **Menorah** <term>The seven-branched candelabra of the Temple, representing the seven lower Sefirot fueled by the light of Wisdom</term> of Wisdom from that passage beyond. This is the **storm of death** <note>original: "sa'arat hamavet" — the chaotic forces of mortality and physical decay</note> of the body, and it awakens the four faces <note>The "four faces" (lion, ox, eagle, man) from Ezekiel's vision, representing the four directions of the created world</note> below. 

The **Righteous one** <term>Tzadik: the spiritual foundation that connects the higher divine realms to the lower physical world</term> in his completeness is like the stirrings of the spirit during the hours of the day. He encountered the peace of the whole ones, and how much shall be, yet it is not found to be perfect in the worlds. Some are of the House, and some are of the work of the House.

Regarding the tranquility of the peaceful ones: lest it be shown below and cease from here, let them not ascend. Each and every one shall be a pillar for his own soul. And this looks back to what returned: not the morning of Wisdom, for Solomon grew silent from the wealth he had taken. He made it outside; we are required to receive the radiance from the meal <note>original: "mis'ada" — refers to the Sabbath meal mentioned on the previous page, which provides spiritual "fuel"</note> without the busy labor of the mundane.

The gracious ones do not skip, nor do they calculate against the law of the House. We are required to take it, for they are tranquil. The Right Hand [of Mercy] praises with compassion, and the speech before them is sharpened. It is a meal for holiness, and it removes the meal of the laborers; and all of us are of the heart, lest it be said of these that it has already returned. For the morning of Wisdom is the source of peace.

He is deficient, and therefore his name is "Lacking," but His Name, may He be blessed, does not lack, nor does His <term>Shleimut</term> <note>Perfection or wholeness; etymologically related to "Shalom" (Peace).</note>. And so, the calculations in the portion of *Kedoshim*... and also, who can understand "Lacking" as opposed to "Perfectly Holy"? To be in the state of "Vitality"—meaning, God forbid, between them all they come into being. And whether they are in a state of "Lacking"—this is the explanation of His work now. Because they are the **Evil Kingdom**, the explanation is that they are not "pious ones," established from the source of the mouth.

Blessed be the name of the Holy One <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu," a standard Aramaic reference to God</note>, blessed be He, forever and for all eternity. ### Bless the Lord, O My Soul
**Bless the Lord, O my soul!** O Lord my God, You are very great; You are clothed in glory and majesty. You wrap Yourself in light as with a garment and stretch out the heavens like a curtain. He lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters; He makes the clouds His chariot and walks upon the wings of the wind. He makes the winds His messengers, and flaming fire His servants.

He established the earth upon its foundations, so that it should never collapse. You covered it with the deep as with a garment; the waters stood above the mountains. At Your rebuke they fled; at the sound of Your thunder they hurried away. They flowed over the mountains and went down into the valleys, to the place You assigned for them. You set a boundary they cannot pass, so they never again cover the earth.

He sends forth springs into the streams; they flow between the mountains. They give drink to every beast of the field; the wild donkeys quench their thirst. Beside them, the birds of the sky have their dwelling; they sing among the branches. He waters the mountains from His upper chambers; the earth is satisfied from the fruit of Your works.

He causes grass to grow for the cattle and vegetation for the service of man, to bring forth food from the earth: wine that gladdens the heart of man, oil to make his face shine, and bread that sustains the human heart. The trees of the Lord are satisfied—the cedars of Lebanon which He planted—where the birds make their nests; as for the stork, the fir trees are her home. The high mountains are for the wild goats; the rocks are a refuge for the hyraxes <note>original: "shfanim," often translated as rock hyraxes or coneys</note>.

He made the moon to mark the seasons; the sun knows its setting. You bring darkness and it becomes night, when all the beasts of the forest prowl. The young lions roar for their prey, seeking their food from God. When the sun rises, they withdraw and lie down in their dens. Then man goes out to his work and to his labor until evening.

**How manifold are Your works, O Lord!** In wisdom You have made them all; the earth is full of Your creations. There is the sea, vast and wide, teeming with creatures beyond number—living things both small and great. There the ships sail, and there is the Leviathan <note>A legendary sea creature representing the untamed aspects of creation</note>, which You formed to play in it.

All of them look to You to give them their food in its proper time. When You give it to them, they gather it; when You open Your hand, they are satisfied with good. When You hide Your face, they are terrified; when You take away their breath, they die and return to their dust. When You send forth Your spirit, they are created, and You renew the face of the earth.

May the glory of the Lord endure forever; may the Lord rejoice in His works. He looks at the earth and it trembles; He touches the mountains and they smoke. I will sing to the Lord as long as I live; I will sing praise to my God while I have my being. May my meditation be pleasing to Him; I will rejoice in the Lord. Let sinners vanish from the earth and the wicked be no more. **Bless the Lord, O my soul. Hallelujah!**

# **"And Joseph harnessed** his chariot" <note>Genesis 46:29</note>. Rabbi Isaac opened [the discourse], and our Rabbis have said:

This teaches us that he would precede [his actions] with **sanctification** <term>Kiddush: A prayer or act of sanctification, here referring to a spiritual preparation</term>, similar to the matter described in the verse: "And he sent Judah before him" <note>Genesis 46:28</note>. 

Regarding this **Midrash** <term>Midrash: Ancient rabbinic commentary and storytelling that interprets biblical texts</term> and the event itself, there are several inquiries. The first is that the word "horse" is missing from the phrase "to his chariot." Furthermore, the word "chariot" appears here in a "construct" form <note>In Hebrew grammar, a word in the 'construct' state is usually linked directly to the following word</note>, which we establish as relating to the three-fold lineage. It should have been written: "And Joseph harnessed the horse to the chariot" <note>original: *sus le-merkavato*</note>.

One must ask why the text is written this way, as it implies a singular vitality. In contrast, it is written of Solomon's horses and chariots that they gather from all the "living creatures" <term>Hayyot: Referring here to the 'Holy Living Creatures' that carry the Divine Chariot in Ezekiel's vision</term>. The animals mentioned here are like the servants who minister to him, and the chariot belongs to her <note>likely referring to the Shekhinah</note> in her daughter-like aspect, and it belongs to her in her perfection. This is not just any vitality, but the vitality of the **Chariot of the Morning Mercies** <note>original: *Merkavet shel Chasdei shel Shachar*</note>, which brings vitality for blessing.

In his heart, he considered this an act of delight and desire, stemming from the "perfect ones" <note>original: *shelamim*</note> who assist him. Thus was his desire, and it provided protection for every helper. Let these "rocks" <note>spiritual foundations</note> be upon their desire and their inner parts. Take these inquiries regarding the "Just Elder" <note>likely referring to Jacob or a personification of the Sefirah of Yesod</note> for the sake of his devotion, which hints at his total surrender, and likewise for all the inner parts of the **Peace Offerings** <term>Shelamim: A category of sacrificial offerings signifying wholeness or peace</term>.

There was a "vitality of life" for Moses arising from sanctification, and it stood before the **Table** <note>likely the Table of the Showbread in the Tabernacle, or a heavenly equivalent</note> as if he were looking ahead to see what the end would be. This sanctification was strengthened through "Hebrew silver" <note>original: *keseph Ivrit*; likely a mystical pun on *kisofin*, meaning spiritual longing or silver coins</note>, which is the "object of vitality." All the structures built by the kings' sons were established upon this. 

The messengers of the "cuttings" <note>possibly referring to the *partzufim* or divine configurations</note> were found within them, and they feel every delight for the three-fold **Peace Offerings**. They wait for the merit in the reckoning. There, the "harnessing of the reins" was performed as one, bound together within **Peace** <note>original: *Shalom*</note>, as it has been explained. 

Every seat at the **Sanctification of the Festival** <note>referring to the Kiddush for a holiday</note> has a "destiny" <note>original: *mazal*; also 'flow' of divine influence</note> within it. There is a subjection to the Holy One, which is missing from ordinary actions. According to the custom of the wise, one binds the **Will** <note>original: *ratzon*</note> to the **Passover** <note>original: *pesach*</note> and to the "Throne of the Meal" <note>the spiritual state attained during a holy feast</note>. This is the vision of the deed, and these are the inquiries of the messengers of the wise.

Indeed, they stand upon the **Throne** <note>original: *karseya*</note> which exists for the sake of the Divine Desire. That particular throne is small, for its purpose is to "break the mouth" [of the accuser] and to fill the belly, as is fitting for a descendant. "Life" implies eternity, for it is meant to be everywhere, a single [unity] for the souls. <meta>catchword: behold</meta>

<meta>This page transitions from the personal narrative and local praises of the previous page into a deep theological and mystical discourse. It seeks to reconcile the philosophical views of Maimonides and Ibn Ezra with the mystical traditions of the Kabbalists regarding the nature of God's knowledge and the role of celestial bodies and angels in governing the world.</meta>

<margin>
Extra strength and hearing the sound of the celestial spheres <note>original: "galgalim," referring to the nested orbits of the planets in ancient cosmology</note> represents the utmost perfection in the aspect of Kingship <term>Malchut: The tenth and final Sephirah (divine emanation), associated with the physical realm and divine presence on earth</term> regarding the "Great Lights." This was explained by the early authorities and the Sages of the Midrash, who were experts in the Book of the Wisdom of Truth <note>meaning the Kabbalah</note>, as written in the Zohar, Part I, page 168b. We have elaborated on this in our composition, "The Commentary on the Pure Menorah," and the wise shall understand. Furthermore, it may be said that "Power" and the "Great Lights" are the Supernal Attributes <term>Middot: The divine emanations or character traits through which God interacts with the world</term> which are called by specific Names. Through this, the opinion of Maimonides (of blessed memory) in *The Guide for the Perplexed* (Part II, Chapter 2) is reconciled with what the Sages of Truth <note>the Kabbalists</note> have spoken on the matter—a hint is sufficient for the wise. So too the opinion of Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra (of blessed memory) as written in his commentary on the Torah for the portion of *Bereishit* <note>Genesis</note>; see there. Through this, the words of the Sages of Truth are well explained. Everything returns to one place, all doubts are settled, and all is upright to the wise of heart who have their eyes in their heads.
</margin>

Perhaps a doubt may fall into the heart of the student, and therefore we preface this for the person of understanding—for the Lord, may He be blessed, is strong, mighty, high, and exalted, and there is no end to His greatness and power. These matters belong to Him—and perhaps through what the Sages of Truth have recounted in this regard, and what they received from the Prophets who spoke in the Name of God, and testified about them concerning all that our Rabbis (of blessed memory) spoke in their teachings and in the lovely Midrash. The ancients called the speakers "Lights," for they have no independent freedom or authority in this matter.

As the eye of the intellect sees that which is known: the Name, may He be blessed, is the Necessary Existent. From Him and under His hand, all things exist through proof and clarity; nothing is too hidden or too wondrous for Him. His knowledge is supreme and perfect; with His wisdom He founded the earth and established the heavens. It is already known regarding the Blessed Name that the **Intellect, the Intelligible, and the Intelligent** <note>original: "HaSekhel, HaMuskal, veHaMaskil." A classic philosophical concept where God is simultaneously the thinker, the object of thought, and the act of thinking</note> are all entirely one single thing. Even though a human being, through their intellect, "acquires" themselves according to their level and becomes the "intelligible" thing, when they are not actively contemplating, they are not the "intelligible." However, regarding the Blessed Name, we say that He is His wisdom and His wisdom is He—and everything before Him is as one single thing. His knowledge does not change at all based on the changes in things external to Him. This is a wondrous thing that the human mind cannot grasp according to the limits of our intellect. From this, the student may understand a little.

Furthermore, our Sages (of blessed memory) noted in the Order of *Moed* and in the first chapter of *Sotah* and in many places, that the Blessed Name "makes peace between the Lights." And regarding what you find in the Talmud concerning the "Supernal Ministers"—the Minister of Fire, the Minister of Water, and the Minister of Rain—and what they said in the Talmud that every single constellation <note>original: "mazal"</note> has a Minister and an Officer ruling over it, and every single star serves before Him.

[Influence is channeled] through the Angel and the Minister appointed over it, who possesses power. Regarding what the Geonim <note>the leaders of Babylonian Jewry, 6th–11th centuries</note> called "the Lights"—referring to the celestial spheres that are appointed over the leadership of the lower world—they first called them "Lights" in terms of the new months and the various constellations. The Holy One, Blessed be He, handed over the leadership of the world, their order, and the order of all the Divine Abundance <term>Shefa: The flow of divine energy or blessing from the upper realms to the lower world</term> coming into the world through the Angels. These are the Separate Intellects <note>non-physical beings</note>, the Spheres, called Seraphim, Living Creatures (*Chayot*), and Sons of God—who [nevertheless] possess a form of matter. These things we have said, being both spiritual and physical, are found in the words of the author of the *Beit Yosef*, the Sages of Inquiry, the Sages of Truth, and the Sages of the Law.

All these matters are correct for one who understands this, and a small portion of our words is enough for them to be able to understand these things in terms of "influence" and "necessity," and the nature of wealth and poverty. They "served the constellation," and that is His knowledge. However, the Sages of Truth called the Sephirot <term>Sephirot: The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite interacts with the universe</term> by these names in the holy *Zohar*, in the *Sefer Ha-Bahir*, and in the *Tikunim*. It is a clear matter among our Rabbis (of blessed memory) that one should not question the "Lights"—which are the Attributes—all of which is proven, and this is enough for the one who understands.

***

So too said Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel <note>15th-century statesman and philosopher</note>, and his son Master Rabbi Judah <note>also known as Leone Ebreo, author of "Dialogues of Love"</note>, and Rabbi Moshe Alsheich <note>16th-century mystic and commentator</note> (may their memory be a blessing). Their explanations dealt with the order of the Lights and the manner of their nourishment from one another. At the conclusion of their words, they explain that among the stars themselves, some receive the power of the Supernal Light, may He be blessed. And some receive from others through the power of the Name dwelling within them. And there are those who turn toward the "External Ones" <term>Chitzonim: In Kabbalah, the "outer" or "other side" representing forces of impurity or judgment</term> and the wicked and Sadducees receive [from there]. Regarding this, the Sages of Truth come to inform us who is who, and which of them is an attribute unto itself, only there to receive and to influence. All these details are found in the "Great Light."

<term>The Great Light</term> for they shall come there. For the sake of the Blessed Name, He provided, and everything proceeds [from Him]. The Spirit of Perfection is to inform us of everything, to know the truth of God and to aim for the truth of the Torah, and to search after the words of our Sages (of blessed memory) to understand the depth of their words, for they are the words of the Living God.
