<meta>This page continues the philosophical and Kabbalistic discourse on the nature of God (the "Perfect One") and the mechanics of creation. It explores the relationship between the active (male) and receptive (female) spiritual forces, drawing on the works of earlier mystics like Naphtali Herz Bacharach to explain how the divine Will manifests in the world.</meta>

When the Perfect One <note>original: *Ha-Shalem* — a philosophical term for God as the ultimate state of completion</note> desires through the perfection found in existence, and when His Will is expressed within the measure of that which exists and its establishment, then the Will and its connection become clarified. Through our own connection, we sustain the rest of existing things. For these, His soul is not renewed <note>i.e., God is not changed by the creation</note>, and because we have explained that the truth is not found in this perfect composite in its own strength, it did not exist until these elements were serving from below in such a way, according to the reason which **Naphtali** <note>referring to Naphtali Herz Bacharach, a 17th-century Kabbalist, specifically his work *Emek HaMelekh* (Valley of the King)</note> mentions in Part B from above. Between these, you will not find the "sickness of deficiency" in the essence of His perfection.

And this is the matter: lest through the preparations, a spring of noble souls emerges; for the Perfect One is the cause of every perfected action, its existence, and its strength. It is because of the existence of the Perfect One from the existing that the mention of their foundation <note>original: *Yesod* — the foundation, also the ninth Sefirah representing the channel of divine vitality</note> was prepared, and likewise to find the Exalted One in His sufficiency. He strengthens their foundation from His own sufficiency. Why does the Exalted One enter the veils of His inquiry? To what end and how does He bring things into existence? Through action and connection, His word shall be; it shall not be otherwise, nor shall its formation be unlike His image. After the inquiry <note>original: *Chakira* — philosophical or mystical investigation</note>, they shall be established. 

Behold, does there not exist before Him a triple strength <note>In Jewish law and mysticism, a "triple strength" or *Chazakah* denotes something that has become permanent and established</note>, more than what is known from His knowledge? Is it not today that they are established? Because of this, the mention of their foundation and their hope stems from that which is known—the bodies that were added, and not the foundation of...

And from time to time as the matter is written: behold, it is seen that a high level and strength are revealed within their foundation. Thus, strength is given to the people from the existence of the [Divine], because the foundation of all of them is lofty from the Female <note>original: *Nukva* — the receptive, feminine aspect of the divine emanations</note> in her holiness, and from that which is after. And there is peace without its kind in holiness, and between the female and the female without the living one who dwells there; this is His praised strength. 

If two hollow vessels <note>original: *nevuvim* — referring to the "vessels" or *Kelium* that receive divine light</note> are found there in peace, we have not yet defined the life of their souls. For every existing thing whose vitality is Male <note>original: *Zakar* — the active, giving principle in Kabbalistic thought</note>, it serves as a "soul" to the Female, until all things are established as Male, which establishes His vitality. He is like dust without the Male, a strong cord of the Perfect One. And the concept of the Female—why is all its hope in the female soul? Lest the testimony of her life be likened to the inner movement of the Will.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the divine mechanics of creation, moving from the philosophical nature of the "Perfect One" into a specific discussion on the nature of Wisdom (Chokhmah) and the mystical significance of Hebrew grammar—specifically the vowels and the figure of Joseph as a channel for divine light.</meta>

Solomon’s wisdom delved deeper than all the people of the East <note>original: *Bnei Kedem*—ancient cultures renowned in the Bible for their esoteric knowledge</note> and the wisdom of Egypt. He reached a supreme level of abstraction within the system of seventy <note>likely referring to the seventy facets of the Torah or the seventy nations of the world</note> to account for them in this manner. Though initially, the lower forces were left above and placed below, their existence descended from the eternal world. They cannot be fully traced in this realm, and if they are denied, their merit will not endure. For this, there is a "still small voice" <note>referring to 1 Kings 19:12, the subtle way God communicates</note> of hearing and precise understanding.

It was written: "Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a spring" <note>original: *Ben porat Yosef, ben porat alei ayin* (Genesis 49:22). In Kabbalah, Joseph represents the *Sefirah* of *Yesod* (Foundation), the channel that brings divine energy into the world</note>. Truly, when the Divine Will desires, it divides itself, separating these elements from those. Yet the connection to God is never severed. As King David said: "[I have quieted] his soul like a weaned child" <note>original: *k'gamul*—the OCR here reads *k'khos* (like a cup), likely a transcription error for the verse in Psalm 131:2</note> and so on. Between the living soul, there is a vision and a precision called "Joseph." On the side of Judgment <note>original: *Din*—the attribute of divine restriction and law</note>, the *Patach* <term>Patach—a Hebrew vowel mark (ַ) representing an "opening" or the expansion of light</term> provides life. Though they may seem to separate, a contracting bond ties everything together. The *Patach* was purified through Joseph, and the image of Wisdom <note>original: *Chokhmah*—the second *Sefirah*, representing pure intuition and the flash of genius</note> was hated <note>possibly meaning "humbled" or "diminished" to allow for creation</note> as it crouched before you.

To give her life, they engrave higher and higher following the Feminine Principle <note>original: *Nukba*—the receptive, creative aspect of the divine</note>. They called out to your hands with that same precision. The *Patach* vowel is the power that gives us life and gives you strength; through this, the world is purified. One who deepens their understanding finds the remnants of the vocalization <note>original: *Nikkud*—the system of dots and lines representing vowels in Hebrew, seen by Kabbalists as the "soul" of the letters</note>. Thus, Joseph provides for her life through the "intentions" of the *Patach*. The one who deepens Wisdom in the lower realms removes the "seventy" <note>the external layers of the nations</note> and binds the *Patach* to life.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of God’s unity and the structure of the cosmos, moving from a critique of secular philosophy to a symbolic and Kabbalistic interpretation of the Psalms and the process of spiritual restoration.</meta>

To offer a parable regarding the one who rectifies <note>original: *metaken*—referring to the process of *Tikkun*, or spiritual repair</note>: There were children in the King’s palace, and they went out one day into the King’s pleasant pastures. Afterward, they became weary and hungry, but they found nothing to eat except a small piece of dry bread. It was given to them in a shameful manner, and it was merely barley bread. Yet, out of respect for the King, they remained silent; they ate and held their peace, though their hearts were heavy because of their meager portion. But in time, they returned to their Father’s house—the King’s palace in its great beauty. There they found a full table set before their Father in His royalty, with every precious thing. He gave them garments of honor, and they began to bless God for the sustenance and the food, their joy now exceeding their previous sorrow. Behold, in the *Psalm of Thanksgiving* <note>original: *Mizmor LeTodah*—Psalm 100</note>, this Psalm is established and stands upon this very mystery through the lens of Understanding <term>Understanding—*Binah*, the third Sephirah, often associated with the "world to come" and the source of redemption</term>. Therefore, if you truly delve deep into this Psalm, you will understand. For at the time the Holy Temple was destroyed, the holy sparks <term>Holy sparks—*Nitzotzin*, the divine light trapped in the material world</term> departed and were scattered among the "external forces" <note>original: *hitzonim*—the demonic or impure realms</note>, God forbid, and they became mixed with filth and famine for all. From that place, that spark which is within the "husk" <term>Husk—*Klippah*, the shell of impurity that conceals divine light</term> was nourished, as was the portion of the wicked. 

But now, they shall cease being nourished by the sustenance of exile, so that the person of Israel may rectify <note>original: *letakhen*</note> the human state, and from there he shall ascend. This is the secret of the "Return" <note>original: *yeshivah*—the returning or sitting</note>, for they have returned to rectify in their distress. They draw down sustenance and divine abundance <note>original: *shefa*</note> through the act of rectification performed for them. This is also the explanation of the Sabbath Psalm <note>likely Psalm 92</note>, for the rhyme of the Psalm is as it was written (and revealed): why this Psalm and this praise, and for what purpose this blessing? The initial letters are "holy" <note>original: *kadosh*</note> from the side of God's Lovingkindness <term>Lovingkindness—*Chesed*, the Sephirah of grace and benevolence</term>. This is the "Firstborn of the Altar" for the Lord, as it is stated in the scripture, and it was fitting for Abraham. And "Isaac shall be blessed" <note>original: *yitbarekh Yitzchak*</note>; may He bless you from across the sea. We shall never lack, and the deficiency of the angels shall be filled from that Unique Lovingkindness—the Kindness of Abraham—which shall be for the obligation of the Sanctuary. There, the children of man shall dwell, fearing the Name and taking refuge in the kindness of their fellow, spreading wings over the faces of the angels. For not every man is clothed in Lovingkindness against transgression. And as for those who did not bring the "Kingship" <note>original: *malkhu*</note> into "Understanding" <note>original: *Binah*</note> for all the sacred service, this is the Rectification of the Morning.

To the student, "moist" <note>original: *lach*</note> implies the meaning of Lovingkindness and the Attribute of Mercy. He concluded with the blessing of the Name and returned to speak of "The One who sustains them." This is the explanation of this Psalm within the sphere of Understanding. This is what my soul intended in understanding these words: the secret of the Holy One of Israel. Oh! For now the time of his yoke has come to be his salvation through mercy, leading to Understanding (and Lovingkindness). As for the Psalm that was not attached—what is it for? It is for the Dedication of the House.

## Rabbi Judah opened and said: "How pleasant are the deeds of this nation! They have established marketplaces,
they have established bridges, they have established bathhouses." Rabbi Jose remained silent. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai responded
and said: "Everything they established, they established only for their own needs. They established marketplaces to station
prostitutes in them; bridges to collect tolls from them; bathhouses to pamper themselves."
Judah, the son of proselytes, went and recounted their words, and they were heard by the Roman government. They said: "Judah,
who elevated [us], shall be elevated; Rabbi Jose, who was silent, shall be exiled to Sepphoris; Shimon, who disparaged, shall be executed."
He and his son went and hid in the House of Study. Every day, his wife would bring him
bread and a jug of water, and they would eat. When the decree became more severe, he said
to his son: "Women are easily swayed; perhaps they will cause her pain and she will reveal us." They went
and hid in a cave. A miracle occurred, and a carob tree and a spring of water were created for them.
They would strip off their clothes and sit up to their necks in the sand. All day they would
study, and at the time of prayer, they would dress so that their clothes
would not wear out. They stayed twelve years in the cave. Elijah came and stood at the entrance
of the cave and said: "Who will inform the son of Yochai that the Caesar has died and his
decree is annulled?" They emerged and saw people sowing and reaping. He said: "They abandon eternal life
and occupy themselves with temporal life!" Every place they cast their eyes was immediately burned. A
Heavenly Voice <term>Bat Kol—literally "Daughter of a Voice," an echo of divine revelation</term> went forth and said: "Have you come out to destroy My world? Return to your cave!" They returned and went
and stayed for twelve months of the year. They said: "The judgment of the wicked in Gehenna <note>original: *Gehinnom*—a place of spiritual purification or punishment in the afterlife</note> lasts twelve months."
A Heavenly Voice went forth and said: "Go out from your cave!" They emerged. Everywhere that
Rabbi Eleazar would strike, Rabbi Shimon would heal.

from the verse 'those who embrace' because of 'from your companion' until he goes out to be heard, for the coming of the Messiah."
